title: Senior Manager, Data Platform - T0
description:
ABOUT AIRWALLEX

Airwallex is the AI-native financial operating system for a real-time, intelligent economy. More than 676,000 businesses, including McLaren Racing, Qantas, SHEIN, and TikTok, use us, directly or through our platform partners, to run their financial operations or build and monetize financial products of their own.

We started in Melbourne in 2015 to build the infrastructure global commerce runs on. We're the regulated backbone behind global payments: not by accident, but by design. A decade plus, 85+ licenses, and a financial infrastructure spanning North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific.

We're co-headquartered in San Francisco and Singapore, with more than 2,300 people across 27 offices. We hire builders with founder-level energy, people who move fast with good judgment, dig in with real curiosity, and make calls from first principles rather than waiting to be told what to do. Read our operating principles https://www.airwallex.com/en-us/operating-principles to see it in full.

 

ABOUT THE TEAM

This team designs intelligent, autonomous systems that eliminate financial operations for companies globally. We automate everything from bookkeeping and reconciliation to tax, payroll, forecasting, and document understanding: turning hours of work into seconds. The team blends deep research pedigree with proven industry experience. We operate with high standards, are tool-agnostic, and expect engineers to own problems end-to-end. We collaborate closely, push boundaries responsibly, and ship exceptional work quickly. You’ll solve unprecedented technical challenges using unique, end-to-end financial datasets no one else in the industry has.

ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Senior Manager of Data Platform Engineering, you’ll lead the team responsible for the data backbone of our financial systems. You’ll set the technical direction for high-volume financial data ingestion, our Databricks lakehouse, data orchestration, canonical financial models, and the infrastructure that makes our data platform reliable, scalable, and increasingly real-time.

You’ll combine strong technical judgment with people leadership-building a high-performing engineering organization, establishing platform standards, driving major migrations, and partnering closely with product, accounting, and platform teams. You’ll help shape a data platform where correctness, auditability, performance, and operational excellence are foundational.

This role is based in San Francisco.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Lead and grow a high-performing data platform engineering team, providing technical direction, mentorship, career development, and clear ownership.

- Set the technical strategy for high-volume financial data ingestion across payment processors, banks, billing systems, and ERP/GL platforms, with strong guarantees around correctness, replayability, and recovery.

- Lead the evolution of our Databricks lakehouse using Spark, Delta Lake, Unity Catalog, dbt, Python, and SQL, optimizing for scale, performance, reliability, and cost.

- Define standards for data contracts, schema evolution, drift detection, data quality, and canonical financial models.

- Evolve the platform from batch toward near-real-time processing using Kafka, CDC, micro-batching, incremental processing, and Dagster orchestration.

- Own the architecture of canonical financial models that transform complex source data into consistent financial objects and relationships powering our accounting engine.

- Partner with infrastructure and platform teams to build reliable production foundations across observability, alerting, incident response, recovery, and operational readiness.

- Guide infrastructure strategy across GCP, Terraform, Kubernetes/GKE, Helm, GitOps, and CI/CD.

- Lead migrations from legacy pipelines to the lakehouse, with rigorous parity validation, staged rollouts, and clear rollback strategies.

- Drive performance and cost optimization across PostgreSQL, Databricks, and lar

title: Senior ML Ops Engineer
description:
Are you a collaborative Machine Learning Ops Engineer looking to work for a mission driven global organization?
Are you looking to drive cutting edge products that have a true societal impact?
About the team, this team that powers Elsevier’s Health platforms: Clinical Key AI, Sherpath AI, and AI-driven automated clinical and content workflows. You will bridge Data Science and Engineering to turn experimental NLP/IR/GenAI models into secure, reliable, and scalable services. Our systems operate over one of the world’s largest medical and scholarly landscapes.
About the role, as a Senior Machine Learning Engineer you’ll work on AI-based features (GenAI, Agentic AI, RAG, etc.) search/ranking quality, and knowledge graph aware retrieval while enforcing content rights and editorial confidentiality.
Key Responsibilities
ML & LLM Engineering, Search and Recommendation Engines

• Automate and orchestrate machine learning workflows across major cloud and AI platforms (AWS, Azure, Databricks, and foundation model APIs such as OpenAI).

• Maintain and version model registries and artifact stores to ensure reproducibility and governance.

• Develop and manage CI/CD for ML, including automated data validation, model testing, and deployment.

• Implement ML Engineering solutions using popular MLOps platforms such as AWS SageMaker, MLflow, Azure ML.

• Scale end-end custom Sagemaker pipelines.

• Design and implement the engineering components of GAR+RAG systems (e.g., query interpretation and reflection, chunking, embeddings, hybrid retrieval, semantic search), manage prompt libraries, guardrails and structured output for LLMs hosted on Bedrock/SageMaker or self-hosted.

• Design and implement ML pipelines that utilize Elasticsearch/OpenSearch/Solr, vector DBs, and graph DBs .

• Build evaluation pipelines: offline IR metrics (NDCG, MAP, MRR), LLM quality metrics (faithfulness, grounding), and A/B testing.

• Optimize infrastructure costs through monitoring, scaling strategies, and efficient resource utilization.

• Stay current with the latest GAI research, NLP and RAG and apply the state-of-the-art in our experiments and systems.

Collaboration

• Partner with Subject-Matter Experts, Product Managers, Data Scientists and Responsible AI experts to translate business problems into cutting edge data science solutions

• Collaborate and interface with Operations Engineers who deploy and run production infrastructure.

Qualifications

• Current experience in ML Engineering, MLOps platforms, shipping ML or search/GenAI systems to production.

• Strong Python, Java, and/or Scala experience will be considered a plus.

• Hands-on‑ experience with major cloud vendor solutions (AWS, Azure and/or Google)

• Experience with Search/vector/graph technologies (e.g., Elasticsearch / OpenSearch / Solr / Neo4j).

• Experience in evaluating LLM models.

• A strong understanding of the Data Science Life Cycle including feature engineering, model training, and evaluation metrics.

• Background in health technology and/or medical content workflows is preferred.

• Familiarity with ML frameworks, e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow, PySpark.

• Experience with large-scale data processing systems, e.g., Spark.

• Experience with statistical analysis, machine learning theory and natural language processing.

Elsevier is a renowned global information analytics company that primarily focuses on providing scientific, technical, and medical (STM) research content, tools, and services. It is one of the largest publishers of academic journals and scholarly literature in the world. Elsevier operates in various domains, including science, technology, medicine, social sciences, and more. They publish a vast number of peer-reviewed journals covering a wide range of disciplines. These journals act as platforms for researchers and academics to share their findings and contribute to the advancement of knowledge in their respective fields.

U.S. National Base Pay Range: $95,300 - $158,800

title: AI Engineer
description:
About Board of Innovation

BOI partners with large, ambitious organizations to design and build applied AI products that create measurable business impact. We help enterprise and scale-up clients move beyond experimentation by embedding AI directly into their operations, decision-making, and products. Our work spans industries, but always centers on production-ready AI, strong engineering, and real-world adoption.
About the Role
We're looking for an AI Engineer to design and build the AI systems behind real, production-grade applications. This is applied engineering work: building agentic workflows, retrieval pipelines, and orchestration layers that integrate into business-critical environments and stand up to real-world use.
You'll take AI capabilities from idea to deployment, owning the full path including evaluation, observability, and the operational concerns that determine whether a system survives contact with users.
What You'll Do
You'll design, implement, and ship AI systems that automate work, support decisions, and unlock new workflows for enterprise clients. Day-to-day, that means building multi-step agents and tool-using LLM systems, wiring them into structured and unstructured data sources, and packaging them into services that other engineers and applications can consume safely.
You'll also own how we know our systems work. That includes evals, observability, and the feedback loops that let us iterate with confidence rather than guesswork. You'll work closely with engineers, strategists, and designers, and you'll be in client conversations from early scoping through delivery.
What You Bring
You have 3+ years of experience shipping AI-powered systems in production, and a background in computer science, math, physics, engineering, or another technical or scientific field. You're strong in Python and fluent in the patterns of modern LLM engineering: agents, MCP, skills, tool use, retrieval, structured outputs, and evals.
You're also a real software engineer underneath. CI/CD, testing, version control hygiene, and code quality matter to you, because they're what let you keep moving fast without things falling over. You understand how to balance accuracy, latency, cost, and maintainability, and you've debugged enough production systems to have opinions about it. You're comfortable wrapping AI logic into services that other engineers can consume without surprises.
How You Work
You treat AI as an engineering discipline. You care about observability, maintainability, and the underlying engineering that makes the interesting parts possible. You're at home in a consulting environment, where each engagement brings a new domain and a new set of constraints.
At BOI, you will work a lot with strategists, designers, and consultants, and most of your clients aren't technical. You're comfortable translating between business problems and technical solutions, and you can hold your own in a client room without a project manager running interference for you.
The field moves quickly, and so do we. New models, new tools, and new patterns show up constantly. You enjoy that pace, actively pull in what's useful, and bring it back to the team. You push back when something doesn't make sense, and you care about building systems that get used long after the kickoff energy fades.
Contract & Setup
We are open to both permanent employment and long-term contractor arrangements. The final setup will depend on your location, work authorization status, and local compliance requirements.
Interested?
If this sounds like a fit, apply with your CV and a short note on a system you've built that you're proud of. Bonus points for something we can actually look at!

title: Security/Compliance SME
description:
This position may be filled prior to the posted deadline. Interested candidates are encouraged to apply as soon as possible. Koniag IT Systems, LLC a Koniag Government Services company, is seeking a Security/Compliance SME with a Secret security clearance to support KITS and our government customer. The position is remote.
Benefits include medical, dental, and vision insurance, 401(k) retirement plan, paid time off, paid parental leave, life and disability insurance, flexible spending accounts, commuter benefits and tuition reimbursement. Koniag IT Systems, LLC a Koniag Government Services company, is seeking an experienced Security / Compliance Subject Matter Expert (SME) to support the Department of the Air Force (DAF) in advancing its enterprise Identity, Credential, and Access Management (ICAM) capabilities. This position will provide dedicated cybersecurity, compliance, and policy expertise across three concurrent System Enhancement Studies under Task Order 0003, covering Contested, Degraded, and Operationally Limited (CDO-L) ICAM environments, Non-Person Entity (NPE) Governance and Management, and the DAF365 Joiner, Mover, Leaver (JML) Transformation Framework. The ideal candidate is a seasoned cybersecurity and compliance professional with deep knowledge of DoD and DAF security policy frameworks, Zero Trust Architecture, and Defense ICAM compliance requirements who can ensure that all study architectural recommendations, governance frameworks, and implementation roadmaps are grounded in current regulatory requirements and defensible against Government security review.

• Note, this is study is for 120 days. All personnel assigned to this effort must hold a final Secret security clearance.
The Security / Compliance SME will serve as the primary authority on cybersecurity policy, regulatory compliance, and security architecture alignment across all three studies within the DAF ICAM System Enhancement Studies effort. Working in close coordination with the Program Manager, Study Lead Engineers, and Identity Architects, the Security / Compliance SME will ensure that every architectural recommendation, governance workflow, and implementation roadmap produced across the three studies is fully aligned with applicable DoD, DAF, and Federal security mandates, Zero Trust requirements, and audit standards. The Security / Compliance SME will contribute substantive compliance and security content to each study's Technical Study Report and will serve as the authoritative reference point for all policy interpretation questions arising during the study period.
Principal responsibilities will include but are not limited to:

• Serve as the authoritative policy and compliance reference across all three System Enhancement Studies, ensuring study outputs are aligned with applicable DoD, DAF, and Federal cybersecurity and identity management mandates throughout the study period.

• Review and interpret all applicable Government-Furnished Information (GFI) and regulatory references relevant to the studies, including NIST SP 800-63 (IAL, AAL, AMR), DoDI 8520.04, DoDI 8510.01, CJCSI 6510.01 audit standards, DAFMAN 17-1304, DAFGM2025-01, DoD/DoW X.509 Certificate Policy, and the DoD Zero Trust Reference Architecture.

• Provide security and compliance guidance to the CDO-L Study Lead Engineer to ensure the CDO-L edge identity architecture, disconnected operational procedures, break-glass access controls, PKI certificate validation approaches, and synchronization methodologies are fully aligned with DoD Zero Trust requirements and applicable classification-level security controls.

• Assess and document security posture management requirements for CDO-L edge node operations, including how endpoint security telemetry integrates with the identity layer and how autonomous access revocation can be enforced in the absence of enterprise policy directives, in alignment with DAF Zero Trust continuous verification requirements.

title: Lead Developer Experience & Infrastructure (m/w/d)
description:
das tun wir
Krankenhäuser sollen sich auf Patienten konzentrieren können, nicht auf administrativen Overhead. Damedic übernimmt den kompletten Prozess der Fallabrechnung: Unsere internen Experten in der medizinischen Kodierung arbeiten Hand in Hand mit unserer KI-basierten Kodierplattform. So gestalten wir die Kodierprozesse von morgen - effizient, zuverlässig und mit menschlichem Fachwissen im Zentrum.
darum brauchen wir dich
KI-native Prozesse verändern grundlegend, was Infrastruktur bedeutet. Was gestern vor allem Infrastructure as Code, Kubernetes und CI/CD was, ist heute die Frage: Wie schaffen wir eine Entwicklungsumgebung, in der KI-Agenten, Automatisierung, internes Wissen und Engineering-Prozesse sicher, sinnvoll und skalierbar zusammenspielen?

Für diese Transformation gibt es keinen Blueprint - Genau hier kommst du ins Spiel. Du übernimmst die Verantwortung und gestaltest diesen Weg aktiv mit - durch kluge Prozesse, nachhaltige Standards, moderne Tools und enge persönliche Zusammenarbeit mit den Teams.

Das erwartet dich

Team-Play & Moderne Developer Experience

•
Führung auf Augenhöhe: Du übernimmst die disziplinarische und fachliche Leitung unseres zweiköpfigen DevEx-Teams. Du verstehst dich als Teamplayer und Enabler, der gemeinsam mit dem Team die Produktivität im gesamten Engineering vorantreibt.

•
DevEx im KI-Zeitalter: Für dich ist DevEx weit mehr als nur lokales Setup und Deployments. Du gestaltest die Rahmenbedingungen für modernes Arbeiten: von Context-Engineering für KI-Agenten über Standards für Skills bis hin zu Entwicklungsprozessen für das Knowledge-Management und die damit verbundenen Tools.

•
Prozesse als Enabler: Du überführst Best Practices in gemeinsame Standards.. Du schaffst Ease of Mind für Entwickler und machst die Organisation als Ganzes effektiver.

•
Messbarer Erfolg: Den Erfolg deiner Arbeit misst du an der Entwicklung des Unternehmens und direktem Feedback, aber eben auch an Key-KPIs wie unserem internen DevEx-Index und DORA-Metriken.

Plattform-Betrieb, Evolution & Automatisierung

•
Betrieb & Cloud: Verantwortung für den stabilen Betrieb unserer AWS/EKS-Landschaft sowie unseres on-premise Systems..

•
Incident- & Alert-Management: Du optimierst den First-Responder-Prozess - u.a. durch Optimierung unseres DevOps-Assistenten.

•
Evolution der Plattform: Kontinuierliche Weiterentwicklung der Infrastruktur zur Stärkung der IT-Security, Etablierung von Best Practices und Optimierung der Cost Efficiency.

•
Compliance & Resilience: Sicherstellung aller Abläufe im Einklang mit unseren Compliance-Zertifizierungen (ISO 27001, BSI C5).

das bieten wir

•
Infrastruktur als Wachstumshebel: Bei Damedic ist Infrastruktur kein reiner Betrieb, sondern ein zentraler Produktivitätshebel für Engineering und Produktentwicklung.

•
Gestaltungsspielraum: Du prägst aktiv, was Developer Experience, Infrastruktur und KI-native Arbeitsweisen bei Damedic künftig bedeuten..

•
Direkte Wirkung: Deine Arbeit beeinflusst unmittelbar, wie schnell, sicher und produktiv unsere Engineering-Teams arbeiten.

•
Healthcare mit Sinn: Unsere Technologie hilft Krankenhäusern, administrativen Aufwand zu reduzieren und mehr Fokus auf Patientenversorgung zu ermöglichen.

•
Remote mit persönlicher Note: Wir arbeiten remote-first innerhalb Deutschlands, übernehmen Kosten für Homeoffice-Ausstattung oder einen Co-Working-Platz, kommen regelmäßig persönlich zusammen und legen auch noch ein Deutschlandticket oben drauf.

so könnte ein tag bei uns aussehen
Morgens analysierst du einen nächtlichen Skalierungsengpass im Cluster: kurzfristig stabilisieren, Ursache verstehen, Monitoring und Architektur verbessern.

Später rollst du ein automatisiertes Dev-Setup breiter aus, sammelst Feedback von Engineers und machst aus einem guten Tool einen genutzten Standard.

In einer Design-Session mit einem Produkt-Team hilfst du, technische Komplexität zu reduzieren und sinnvolle Standardkomponenten statt Eigenbau einzusetzen.

• Knowledge of pharmaceutical industry, regulatory process, clinical trials and medical terminology

• Business Experience - Experience working in a clinical research environment (within a SMO, CRO, sponsor, site) and a deep understanding of the oncology clinical research setting is strongly preferred.

• Knowledge and interpretation of clinical research protocols, and experience in a clinical setting analyzing patient charts is required.

Skills: The proficiency to perform a certain task.

• Attention to detail, solid execution, meeting aggressive timelines, strong interpersonal skills and team player. Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

• Documented training, knowledge and application of current FDA Regulations, GCP and ICH guidelines in clinical trials.

• Ability to collaborate effectively with the study team, cross functional team members and external partners (including investigators and site staff) using collaborative negotiation skills.

• Excellent organizational and priority management skills.

• Strong computer skills including knowledge of Microsoft Excel, Word, PowerPoint and Outlook.

• Ability to work within established timelines, in a fast-paced environment.

The first thing someone experiences when they arrive at a building sets the tone for everything that follows. You're that first thing.

As a Lobby Ambassador, your job is to make arrivals and departures feel smooth, welcoming, and professional. You greet tenants by name, manage the visitor check-in process, answer questions about the building, and make sure the lobby always looks and feels the way it should.

This is a hospitality role grounded in consistency. The value you create isn't in occasional big moments - it's in showing up the same way every single day, so tenants know exactly what to expect when they walk through the door.

title: Senior Power Controls Engineer
description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

Anduril is seeking an experienced Power Controls Engineer to develop and implement advanced control algorithms for high-performance power electronic systems. We're looking for someone with deep expertise in control system modeling and simulation - particularly in Simulink and PLECS - who can take a controls concept from simulation through hardware validation. This individual will own the control architecture for DC/DC converters, inverters, and motor drives built around discrete SiC and GaN power stages, and will work closely with power hardware and firmware engineers to deliver tightly integrated, high-reliability systems for defense and aerospace applications.

WHAT YOU'LL DO:

• Design, simulate, and validate closed-loop control algorithms for switch-mode power converters and inverters using Simulink and/or PLECS.

• Controls for 3-phase AC systems, with and without a switched Neutral

• Develop plant models and controller architectures (voltage-mode, current-mode, sensorless FOC, etc.) for multi-kW power stages utilizing discrete SiC and GaN FETs.

• Perform stability analysis, loop shaping, and compensator design to meet transient response, efficiency, and EMI targets.

• Collaborate with power hardware engineers on gate drive tuning, dead-time optimization, and switching-loss characterization of wide-bandgap devices.

• Support model-based code generation workflows and work with firmware engineers to translate control designs into embedded implementations.

• Define and execute hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) and power-hardware-in-the-loop (PHIL) test plans to validate control performance against system requirements.

• Contribute to trade studies on converter topology, modulation strategy, and control bandwidth as they relate to size, weight, power, and thermal constraints.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:

• BS in Electrical Engineering, Controls Engineering, or related discipline.

• 8+ years of experience designing and tuning digital control loops for power electronic converters (DC/DC, DC/AC, or motor drives).

• Proficiency in Simulink and/or PLECS for control system modeling, simulation, and analysis.

• Strong foundation in control theory - z-domain and s-domain design, bode analysis, state-space methods, and discrete-time implementation considerations.

• Hands-on experience with discrete SiC and/or GaN FET-based power stages in the multi-kW range.

• Familiarity with military or aerospace environments and standards such as MIL-STD-461, 464, 810, or DO-160.

• Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

• MS/PhD with a focus in power electronics controls or control systems.

• Experience writing embedded firmware (C/C++) for microcontrollers or DSPs used in power converter control (e.g., TI C2000, STM32).

• Familiarity with auto-code generation from Simulink (Embedded Coder) or similar model-based design toolchains.

• Experience with real-time HIL platforms (e.g., Typhoon HIL, dSPACE, OPAL-RT).

• Knowledge of advanced modulation techniques (SVM, DPWM) and their impact on switching losses in wide-bandgap devices.

• Design-for-Reliability practices including DFMEA.

• Experience with EMI mitigation strategies at the controls and layout level.

title: Technical Writer
description:
TL;DR: Most companies treat documentation as a help centre. At Lovable it's part of the product. Millions of people learn to build software from our docs, and so do the AI agents working for them: the Lovable agent suggests pages, coding tools read them, and our assistants answer from them. You'll be our second technical writer, with product areas of your own from the start and a seat at every launch, and you'll help work out something nobody has fully worked out yet: what documentation should be when its readers are people and agents, and the product changes every day.

Why Lovable?

Lovable is the software creation platform that gives people the power to act on the problems closest to them. For decades, turning an idea into software required so much capital, technical fluency, and time that many ideas never came to life. Lovable is the counterargument: a platform for all people with ideas, ambition, and problems worth solving. From solopreneurs to small business owners to teams at companies like Adidas and Zendesk, people have built over 60 million projects on Lovable since its launch in November 2024. And we're just getting started.

We're building a generational company from Stockholm, with growing teams in London, Boston, New York, and San Francisco. Our team is small, talent-dense, and moving quickly, with a culture rooted in extreme ownership, high velocity, and low-ego collaboration. We look for people who care deeply, ship fast, and are eager to make a dent in the world.

Lovable is one of TIME's 100 Most Influential Companies and has been recognized on the Forbes AI 50 and CNBC Disruptor 50, reflecting our momentum as one of Europe's fastest-growing AI companies and one of the most ambitious places to build in this next era of software.

What we're looking for

- You've spent 3+ years documenting software products, and you can show us pages that get a reader to the outcome without re-reading.

- You already write with AI: for research, drafting and checking, not just polish. You know what it gets wrong and you catch it.

- You test what you document. You'd rather try the feature and read the source than take someone's word for it, and when something's broken or confusing, you say so.

- You're at home in docs-as-code: Git, Markdown and pull requests.

- You ask engineers and PMs specific questions, and when documenting a feature shows it won't make sense to users, you raise it early, with reasons.

- Preferred: you've shipped docs weekly at a startup or scale-up, finding out what changed yourself. You've written for AI readers, or you're curious about it. You have UX writing or content design experience, or an interest in it. You can read code well enough to check how a feature actually behaves; writing code is not required.

What you'll do

- Drive, don't wait. Features land every day, and bigger launches several times a month. You find out what's shipping before anyone tells you, and the docs are ready the day it ships.

- Own it end to end. Work a feature out from the code and the product, write the page, verify it in Lovable, ship it, and keep it true as the product moves.

- Care about the reader more than the feature. Our docs come with data: what people can't find, what the assistant couldn't answer, what support hears. You use it to decide what to write next.

- Make the product better, not just explain it. Documenting a feature means using it end to end. You'll find the confusing label or the broken step and get it fixed before launch.

- Write for three readers on one page. The non-technical builder, the developer, and the AI agent working on their behalf.

- Build something that outlasts the week. AI drafts a lot of our pages. The human work is judgement: what a feature needs, what the engineer didn't mention, and the checks that keep hundreds of pages correct.

- Where you'll start:

- Enterprise. Identity and access, governance, audit, data residency: the pages a security team reads before they sign.

title: Experiential Producer
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

AI will change how the world works. Human connection will shape what it becomes. OpenAI’s Events and Experiences team, part of Business Marketing, carries the critical responsibility of bringing people together around OpenAI’s mission - building artificial general intelligence that benefits all of humanity. We strive to put human benefit in the spotlight and craft experiences that build trust, spark possibility, and make the future feel within reach and exciting. We are not a traditional events team: we move with extreme speed, rigor, and precision. We use AI tools to rethink everything from the first plan to the final guest moment - and we bring grit, joy, humor, and extraordinary creative talent to create what has not existed before.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for an Experiential Producer to put OpenAI’s latest technology in people’s hands. You’ll produce experiences where people discover something they didn’t know they could do with our products, whether they’re trying ChatGPT for the first time or building with our newest developer tools. From intimate demos to global launches, cultural programs, large-scale events, booths, and brand installations, you’ll help shape how people experience OpenAI around the world.

Working closely with Product, Marketing, and creative partners, you’ll take concepts through design development, fabrication, and on-site delivery. You’ll bring deep experience producing booths and custom builds, managing agencies and vendors, and working directly with fabricators to understand what’s possible within the budget and timeline.

This role needs someone who can run several projects at once and stay close to the details. You’re resourceful when plans change, comfortable making decisions on your feet, and clear with the people depending on you. You take pride in producing great work and bring a sense of humor and genuine enthusiasm to the process.

IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

- Produce the experiences that introduce people to OpenAI’s newest products, from global launches and hands-on demos to custom installations around the world.

- Work with Product, Marketing, and creative teams on what’s coming next, turning ambitious concepts into production briefs and build plans for different audiences.

- Bring together agencies, fabricators, technical specialists, and venues to solve builds that don’t have an off-the-shelf answer, from early prototypes to finished experiences.

- Independently run several projects at once. Set milestones and own scopes, bids, negotiations, contracts, procurement, budgets, and forecasts while keeping deadlines, dependencies, and approvals organized.

- Lead booth builds, technical production, and live delivery, from product integrations and AV to show calls. Protect quality, accessibility, safety, privacy, and brand standards.

- Keep a fast-moving team informed and supported. Celebrate wins, share progress and hurdles without prompting, and take on unfamiliar problems as plans change.

- Experiment with OpenAI tools throughout production, from research and planning to vendor briefs, project updates, and post-event analysis. Help the team find better ways to work.

- Set success measures and use audience response, product engagement, business results, and partner feedback to improve future experiences, reusable production tools, and vendor standards.

YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU HAVE:

- 8+ years producing experiential programs, brand activations, launches, installations, exhibitions, or live events, ideally for technology or complex products.

- Deep experience producing booths and custom builds, with a portfolio showing sound design judgment, practical problem-solving, and careful execution.

- Experience working with Product, Engineering, or technical teams, and genuine curiosity about how OpenAI’s products work.

- The initiative to own projects independently: set milestones, make decisions, and tackle unfamiliar problems without waiting to be aske

title: Technical Project Manager
description:
Technical Project Manager
Location: Remote
Multiple clients. Moving parts. You keep it all connected.
We're looking for a Technical Project Manager who can manage multiple client-facing projects simultaneously, keep technical teams aligned, and give clients confidence that their projects are in good hands.
You're comfortable discussing requirements with developers, translating technical details into plain English, and keeping scope, timelines, and priorities under control. You bring structure, communicate clearly, and address problems before they become surprises.
What You'll Do

• Manage multiple client projects from discovery and kickoff through development, testing, launch, and handoff.

• Serve as the primary project contact for clients, providing clear updates and setting realistic expectations.

• Turn client goals into actionable requirements, project plans, milestones, and deliverables.

• Track scope, schedules, budgets, resources, and dependencies across concurrent projects.

• Identify risks early, resolve blockers, and escalate issues with recommended solutions.

• Manage change requests and explain their impact on cost, timing, and delivery.

• Lead productive kickoff meetings, sprint planning, status calls, demos, and retrospectives.

• Partner with technical leads to ensure deliverables meet requirements and acceptance criteria.

• Maintain clear documentation and improve processes as you learn what works.

What You Bring

• Proven experience managing multiple client-facing technical projects at the same time .

• A track record of delivering software, web, application, or technology implementation projects.

• Working knowledge of software development lifecycles, Agile/Scrum, and traditional project management approaches.

• Enough technical fluency to discuss APIs, integrations, databases, and deployment requirements with technical teams.

• Strong client communication skills, including the ability to navigate difficult conversations and competing priorities.

• Excellent organization, follow-through, and attention to detail.

• Experience using tools such as Jira, Asana, ClickUp, Monday.com, or similar platforms.

• The ability to work independently and coordinate distributed teams in a remote environment.

Bonus Points

• Experience in a digital agency, software consultancy, or other environment serving multiple clients.

• Experience with resource planning, project financials, or statements of work.

• PMP, Certified ScrumMaster, or a similar certification.

What Success Looks Like
Clients know where their projects stand. Teams understand what needs to happen next. Risks surface early, changes are handled thoughtfully, and projects reach the finish line with quality and accountability.
If you can connect the technical details, the client relationship, and the delivery plan, we'd love to hear from you.

title: AI Agent Engineer, Workforce Experience
description:
Company Overview

Orbis is a technology company that delivers sovereign intelligence and decision capabilities to the United States Government and its allies. We convert complex information and operational systems into decisive outcomes, giving public institutions and critical enterprises the tools to move faster, see clearer, and act first in an increasingly contested world.

We are not a consulting firm and not a systems integrator. Every Orbis team is built around practitioners who have operated at the mission edge, and every engagement is judged on one thing: whether it produces working capability, not slide decks. Solutions forged from experience; that is how we build, and it is how we hire.

Job Summary
Orbis is building the agentic AI capability its operations run on, and the AI Agent Engineer builds and operates it. Sixty percent of this role is common to every AI Agent Engineer at Orbis: designing, building, and deploying the multi-agent workflows behind triage, data retrieval, summarization, reporting, and escalation routing. The remaining forty percent is this role's focus - how Orbis employees get their work done with AI. This engineer builds the internal tooling, owns intake and self-service, and drives the adoption and enablement that determine whether the capability is used or ignored.
Travel: Occasional (up to 10%) to McLean, VA or team offsites as needed
Key Responsibilities - Common Core (60% of the Role)
Every AI Agent Engineer at Orbis, regardless of focus area, owns the following:

•
Design, build, and deploy agentic AI workflows. Architect and ship the multi-agent and automated workflows that run in production: triage, data retrieval, summarization, reporting, and escalation routing.

•
Translate in both directions. Explain to non-technical stakeholders what the systems do, where they are reliable, and where they are not, in terms those stakeholders can act on. Equally, take a process owner's plain-language description of how their work happens and turn it into a workflow specification that holds up.

•
Partner with process owners to build what they actually need. Work directly and iteratively with the colleagues who own a process so the resulting capability fits their operation rather than forcing them to fit it. Push back constructively when a stated requirement will not survive contact with production.

•
Keep the workflows reliable. Monitor what is running in production, diagnose failures across prompts, tools, data, and orchestration, and resolve them. Know which problems are yours to solve and when to bring in engineering.

•
Own the cost of execution. Track what your AI workloads cost to run. Identify where a tighter prompt, a caching layer, or a simple deterministic step delivers the same outcome, and keep those costs defensible as volume grows.

•
Set the quality bar for AI-assisted output. Define accuracy standards, human review checkpoints, and escalation criteria for the automated workflows, and build the checks that prove those standards are being met.

•
Document what you build. Author and maintain the runbooks and SOPs that allow others to operate and troubleshoot these workflows without you. Nothing lives only in one person's head.

•
Integrate across Orbis products. Work across Catalyst, Pulse, and Discovery, with engineering support where needed, so workflows can access and act on the data they require.

•
Deliver the reporting leadership and the team depend on. Build and maintain the outputs behind resolution rate, escalation rate, output accuracy, response time, and employee satisfaction, and turn the Senior Operations Manager's requirements into structured, recurring reports and data exports.

•
Close capability gaps and keep the practice current. Recognize when a need is not served by existing tooling, scope the gap clearly, and either build it or bring it to engineering and product with enough detail to act on. Track developments in agentic AI tooling and enterprise automation platf

title: Collecte de données vocales – France et outre-mer
description:
En quoi consiste le projet ?
L’objectif de ce projet vise à collecter des enregistrements vocaux de personnes de langue maternelle française afin d’améliorer les technologies d’assistant vocal.
Description de la tâche :
Pour ce projet, nous recherchons une grande variété de locuteurs natifs de langue française (France et outre-mer) avec divers accents régionaux. Les participants enregistreront de courtes phrases d’activation et des énoncés scriptés généralement utilisés lors d’interactions avec un assistant vocal, en suivant les instructions fournies.
Qui peut participer à l’étude ?
Pour participer, vous devez remplir les conditions suivantes :

• Avoir 18 ans ou plus.

• Être né(e) et vivre en France ou outre-mer.

• Être de langue maternelle française, de n’importe quelle région de France ou outre-mer.

• Avoir une bonne maîtrise de l’anglais, car toutes les instructions du projet seront en anglais.

• Être en mesure d’utiliser un téléphone portable pour ce projet.

• Pouvoir utiliser un casque filaire ou le microphone de l’appareil pour enregistrer des phrases.

•
Avoir accès à un environnement intérieur calme pour effectuer les enregistrements.

Notes:

• Dans le cadre de ce projet, nous recherchons des participants issus de groupes démographiques spécifiques afin de contribuer au développement d’une technologie impartiale qui soit représentative de tous. Certains groupes sont déjà complets, mais nous recherchons toujours des voix masculines avec des accents du Nord, du Nord-est, du Sud-ouest et du Sud-est de la France.

• Nous recherchons aussi des participants issus d’outre-mer: Guadeloupe (971), Martinique (972), Guyane (973), La Réunion (974), Mayotte (976), Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon (975), Saint-Barthélemy (977), Saint-Martin (978), Wallis-et-Futuna (986), Polynésie française (987), Nouvelle-Calédonie (988), Terres australes et antarctiques françaises (984) et Clipperton (989).

Veuillez noter que ce projet est également ouvert aux participants âgés de 7 à 17 ans . Pour plus de détails, veuillez vous référer à ce formulaire :Gardenia Speech Collection - France (Minors) | DataForce Community
Où le projet a-t-il lieu ?
C’est un projet entièrement à distance. Vous pouvez participer depuis n’importe où en France ou outre-mer.
Combien de temps dure-t-il ?
La durée estimée de la tâche d’enregistrement est de 30 minutes.
Quel est le montant de la rémunération ?
Vous recevrez $ 33 USD pour vos livrables entièrement terminés et acceptés.
Programme général de prime de parrainage
Nous offrons une prime de parrainage de $ 15 USD pour chaque participant adulte que vous recommandez pour le projet et qui le termine avec succès.
Comment parrainer quelqu’un :
- Partagez ce lien d’inscription avec vos amis et votre famille
- Lors de leur inscription, ils doivent répondre « Referral» (Recommandation) à la question « How did you find out about this opportunity? » (Comment avez-vous pris connaissance de cette opportunité ?) et indiquer votre nom et votre adresse e-mail dans les champs : Prénom, Nom et adresse e-mail.
Comme mode de paiement, nous proposons le Virement bancaire, PayPal et la Carte cadeau , selon votre préférence.
Veuillez noter que notre équipe d’assurance qualité examinera toutes les soumissions pour s’assurer qu’elles respectent les exigences spécifiques du projet. L’équipe du projet vous enverra des commentaires une fois le processus de contrôle qualité terminé.
Des questions ou des doutes ?
Si vous avez des doutes ou des questions, n’hésitez pas à nous contacter à:
Si vous souhaitez participer et que vous remplissez les conditions d’éligibilité ci-dessus, veuillez cliquer sur Postuler ici et remplir le formulaire d’inscription.

title: Senior Site Reliability Engineer
description:
About Mozn
MOZN is a leading Enterprise AI company enabling organizations to make informed decisions in two critical domains: Financial Crime Prevention and Enterprise Knowledge Intelligence.

We’re a diverse, collaborative team of innovators united by a shared purpose: to build AI that delivers tangible business value, builds trust, and empowers people and organizations with augmented intelligence. Our culture is built on the relentless pursuit of excellence and meaningful impact.

If you’re passionate about working alongside exceptional talent on world-class AI, and you want the autonomy and runway to do the best work of your career, join us in shaping the future of intelligent enterprises.
About the role
We're hiring an AI Senior SRE: someone who carries a normal SRE workload - on-call rotation, incident response, root cause analysis, hands-on Kubernetes/cloud work - and builds the agentic layer that automates that workload over time. You are not exempt from operating production. You're the person best placed to know what should be automated, because you're the one doing it. This role exists because most reliability toil (triage, root-causing, remediation, SLO tracking, onboarding checks) is repetitive and well-defined enough to hand to an LLM-based agent with the right guardrails. Your job is to do the on-call/ops work like any SRE, then turn what you learn into agents - identify the workflow, build the agent, and earn the trust to let it act with increasing autonomy.
What you'll do

• Carry a normal on-call rotation and act as a hands-on responder: investigate, fix, and document incidents yourself, exactly like any SRE on the team - especially for workflows that don' t have an agent yet.

• Go deep on application-level reliability, not just infrastructure: read and debug service code, understand business logic well enough to find the real root cause, and ship fixes or PRs directly into application repos when the fix belongs in the app, not the platform.

• Design, build, and ship LLM-based agents (using tools like Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, or Kimi K2/K3) that plug into our existing stack: Kubernetes, cloud APIs, Prometheus/Grafana/ELK/Datadog, PagerDuty/Slack.

• Define the "tool" interface each agent needs - the specific APIs, scripts, and read/write actions - and build safe wrappers around them.

• Set clear guardrails for every agent: what it may do autonomously vs. what it must propose for human approval, with a bias toward human-in-the-loop until an agent has earned trust.

• Own agent evaluation - define what "correct" and "safe" look like per agent, and build test/backtest suites against real historical incidents.

• Continuously tune prompts, context, and tool schemas as an agent' s scope grows.

• Partner with the SRE/platform team to find good agent candidates: repetitive, well-scoped, auditable workflows.

• Report on agent impact - MTTD/MTTR/MTTX movement, false positive/negative rates, and engineer-hours of toil removed.

• Keep a security- and compliance-first posture: audit trails for every autonomous action, least-privilege access to production, and alignment with Saudi data residency/regulatory requirements.

Requirements

• 3+ years building production software with LLMs - agentic workflows, tool/function calling, multi-step planning, RAG - not just personal use of a chat assistant.

• Hands-on experience shipping real work with an agentic coding tool such as Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, or Kimi K2/K3.

• Strong Python (or similar) for building agent tooling, API wrappers, and orchestration.

• Real, hands-on SRE experience: comfortable being a primary on-call responder, running incident response, and doing root cause analysis under pressure - not just familiar with the concepts.

• Application-level debugging skill, not just infra: able to read a service' s codebase, trace a failure back to the actual line/logic causing it, and ship a fix yourself - SRE work here isn' t limited to restarting pods or scal

The Medical Science Liaison (MSL), Rare Disease is a field-based scientific expert and a key scientific resource for clinicians, academic institutions, and professional organizations in the Rare Disease community. This individual builds relationships with Key Opinion Leaders (KOLs), leads scientific exchange on Natera's Rare Disease test, and brings field insights back to Rare Disease leadership. The MSL works closely with the Rare Disease Sales, Marketing, and Medical teams to help bring the test to more patients. This role operates with a high degree of autonomy and reports to the Director of MSLs, Rare Disease.

PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Provide scientific and clinical presentations on Natera products, with a focus on Rare Disease, and respond to customer requests for information about marketed and developing products.

• Must pass a post-offer criminal background check.

• Knowledge of Rare Disease and relevant clinical sciences, with the ability to explain clinical laboratory test data to clinicians.

• Working knowledge of HIPAA, PHI, and medical compliance standards.

• Scientific writing and data analysis skills.

Behavioral:

• Independent thinker who works with autonomy and manages priorities in a field-based role.

title: Engineering Lead, Air Defense U.S. Air Force Portfolio
tags: AFS : Air Defense Engineering : Chief Engineering
description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Anduril's Air Defense team develops, integrates, and fields autonomous systems that find, track, and defeat threats in the sky while keeping operators in control of engagement decisions. The team brings together Roadrunner, Sentry, Anvil, Pulsar, and Wisp with existing and third-party sensors and effectors through Lattice, creating a software-enabled family of systems for the modern battlespace. As control of the air becomes more contested, these networked capabilities give warfighters the awareness and response options needed to protect forces against rapidly evolving UAS threats.

ABOUT THE JOB

The U.S. Air Force is one of Anduril's largest and fastest-growing air defense customers, and the work has moved well past demonstrations. The portfolio runs programs of record, multi-year IDIQs, and recurring sustainment at the same time, and installation defense is scaling from individual sites toward a service-wide posture. The technical scope is broadening with it, across sensors, effectors, command and control, tactical networks, and accreditation boundaries.

Four kinds of work run in parallel. Permanent installations defend flightlines and test ranges on base infrastructure under a government accreditation posture, which makes power, networking, cyber compliance, and data handling as much of the engineering as sensors and effectors. Deployable kits ship on short notice and have to work on arrival, including in environments cold enough to change how the hardware behaves. Rapidly relocatable passive detection pushes the kill chain well past the base perimeter and into the theater air picture through tactical data links. And part of the portfolio executes inside special access environments, where the engineering includes constraining what the system is permitted to disclose.

You are the engineering lead across all of it. You own the technical baseline for the delivered configurations in the portfolio: the architecture, the interfaces to Anduril and third-party sensors and effectors, the networks underneath them, the accreditation scope, and the verification approach that determines whether any of it is ready. Where individual programs carry their own systems engineers, you hold the picture that spans them and settle the technical questions that fall between owners.

The work is broad by design. A given week might be reconciling environmental requirements that conflict across a contract and a test plan, defining the interface to a partner's fielded command and control, writing the technical content behind a proposal, or standing on a flightline because a site is not performing and the answer is not in the logs. The portfolio is growing faster than its engineering bench, so the role carries real latitude over where the engineering effort goes.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Own the technical baseline. Architecture, interface set, and verification approach for the delivered configurations across the portfolio. Set the baseline for each, and update it when field evidence shows the current one is incomplete or wrong. Own the certification and accreditation scope where it applies, working with the teams responsible for those functions.

description:
About Lowry Research
Founded in 1938 and acquired by CFRA in 2021, Lowry Research provides independent technical market analysis to investment professionals. Our proprietary methodology uses daily price and volume data from NYSE and Nasdaq-listed stocks to evaluate market supply and demand, identify trends, and assess market conditions. This temporary, part-time Technical Research Analyst position offers an opportunity to contribute to Lowry Research's proprietary technical research for Lowry and CFRA clients globally.

This is a fully remote, temporary position based in the United States, expected to last approximately two months at 25 hours per week.

We are looking for someone who can start as soon as possible.

Key Responsibilities

• Perform technical market analysis using Lowry Research's proprietary data, indicators, and methodology.

• Prepare daily market commentary and regular technical research reports covering market trends, sectors, industry groups, ETFs, and individual equities.

• Monitor and interpret market breadth, volume, momentum, relative strength, and other technical indicators.

• Support Senior Analysts in identifying market trends and developing technical research themes.

• Assist with recurring research publications, market updates, and data analysis.

• Maintain research databases and indicators, supporting improvements and automation where applicable.

• Collaborate with technical and fundamental research teams and participate in internal meetings as needed.

Skills, Knowledge and Expertise

• Bachelor's degree in Finance, Economics, Business, or a related field preferred.

• Chartered Market Technician (CMT) designation or progress toward certification preferred.

• Demonstrated experience in technical market analysis or investment research incorporating technical indicators.

• Experience analyzing market breadth, volume, momentum, trend, and relative strength indicators across equities, ETFs, sectors, and industry groups.

• Experience writing investment research reports, market commentary, or other financial publications.

• Strong analytical, writing, and Microsoft Excel skills, with proficiency in Word and PowerPoint.

• Ability to interpret market data, identify trends, and communicate findings clearly and concisely.

• Strong attention to detail, organizational skills, and ability to work independently and collaboratively in a remote environment.

Nationally recognized nonprofit venture philanthropy seeks to hire an Associate Partner on the Innovative Public Schools Team to find, fund, and support leaders designing the next generation of innovative, future-ready public schools in K-12 education.

NewSchools is a venture philanthropy that builds a better education system by connecting people, resources, and ideas. We bridge the gap between those with capital and those with the courage to put that capital to work on the frontlines of K-12 education. We envision an education system that keeps its promise to all students. That’s why we invest in the ideas and energy of education leaders and entrepreneurs who are advancing innovative solutions that expand the definition of what works. There’s a better way to advance education through philanthropy-one that is more equitable, more collaborative, and more courageous-and we’re proving it every day.

The Innovative Public Schools (IPS) team at NewSchools Venture Fund seeks an Associate Partner (AP) to lead our work finding and supporting school founders building future-ready school models. In this role, you will hold a portfolio of up to 10 public school teams in the design phases, roughly two years before opening, and lead our new work supporting AI-native and AI-supported fresh start schools. You will spend meaningful time in the field learning how innovation is showing up in schools and bringing that learning back to evolve our strategy. Contribute to IPS’ AI schools work

• Serve as the IPS lead for identifying, selecting, and supporting AI-native and AI-supported fresh start schools, setting the bar for what counts as AI built into a model’s core design versus AI used as an added tool.

description:
Qui sommes-nous ?
Télécom Paris, école de l’IMT (Institut Mines-Télécom) et membre fondateur de l’Institut Polytechnique de Paris, est une grande école du top 6 des écoles d’ingénieurs généralistes françaises.
La Raison d’Être de Télécom Paris est de former, imaginer et entreprendre pour concevoir des modèles, des technologies et des solutions numériques au service d’une société et d’une économie respectueuses de l’humain et de son environnement.

Nous recherchons une Post-doctorante ou un Post-doctorant en fondements quantiques et méthodes algébriques pour rejoindre le département INFRES à Télécom Paris.

Le poste est accueilli au sein de Quriosity, équipe commune à Inria et Télécom Paris, au laboratoire LTCI et au département Informatique et Réseaux (INFRES). Située à Palaiseau, sur le plateau de Saclay, l’équipe bénéficie d’un environnement actif en information quantique et en fondements de la théorie quantique.
Le recrutement relève du projet PIQ « Nouveaux outils algébriques pour les décompositions causales des processus quantiques », sous la responsabilité d’Augustin Vanrietvelde. Il porte sur la phase 1 du projet, pour une durée de 18 mois.
Le projet étudie la conjecture des décompositions causales : tout canal unitaire admettrait une décomposition dont les connexions reflètent fidèlement sa structure causale. L’objectif est de développer des outils algébriques et syntaxiques pour étudier des cas ouverts, construire des décompositions ou identifier des obstructions. La recherche est exploratoire ; les résultats partiels et les limites des méthodes seront documentés.

Vos principales missions seront de :
Mener des recherches sur les décompositions causales des processus quantiques dans le cadre de la phase 1 du projet PIQ.
Assurer des missions d’encadrement et de tutorat de projets étudiants et de stages.
Contribuer au rayonnement scientifique de Télécom Paris, de l’Institut Mines-Télécom et de l’Institut Polytechnique de Paris.

Vous êtes titulaire d’un doctorat ou équivalent en physique, mathématiques, informatique ou dans une discipline pertinente pour le projet, obtenu au plus tard à la prise de fonctions.
Vous devez posséder de solides connaissances en fondements quantiques, notamment en causalité quantique, ou en méthodes algébriques avancées, ainsi que de bonnes capacités de raisonnement mathématique, de démonstration et d’analyse critique. Vous devez être autonome dans la conduite de recherches théoriques, savoir rédiger des travaux scientifiques rigoureux et maîtriser l’anglais scientifique, à l’écrit comme à l’oral.
Des connaissances en algèbres d’opérateurs, en information quantique et en formalismes diagrammatiques sont souhaitées. Une expérience en calcul symbolique ou numérique appliqué à des problèmes théoriques, ainsi qu’en encadrement d’étudiants, constitue un atout. Enfin, vous devez faire preuve d’un bon esprit d’équipe, de capacités de dialogue et de synthèse, ainsi que de solides qualités rédactionnelles et pédagogiques.

Pourquoi nous rejoindre ?
Vous travaillerez dans un environnement en plein développement, agréable, verdoyant et accessible (notamment pour les personnes en situation de handicap) à seulement 20 km de Paris (RER B et C, proximité des grands axes routiers).

• flexibilité des horaires de travail (en fonction de l'activité du service)

• télétravail 1 à 3 jours/semaine possible

title: Technical Recruiter
description:
ABOUT MERCOR

Mercor's mission is to organize human intelligence to power the AI economy. We're a leading AI data company, building the layer between human expertise and frontier models. Millions of domain experts on the platform are paid over $4 million per day to train frontier AI models. Mercor's APEX benchmark family measures AI's real-world impact on professional work. Mercor Enterprise brings this same infrastructure to Fortune 500 companies: helping companies capture how their best people actually work, translating that expertise directly back into agents.

 

Mercor is creating a new category of work where expertise powers AI advancement. Achieving this requires an ambitious, fast-paced and deeply committed team. You’ll work alongside researchers, operators, and AI companies at the forefront of shaping the systems that are redefining society. Mercor is a profitable Series C company valued at $10 billion. We work in-person five days a week in our San Francisco, NYC, or London offices.

ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Technical Recruiter at Mercor, you’ll own full-cycle hiring across critical technical functions, partnering directly with the VP of Engineering, CTO, and engineering leadership. You’ll play a foundational role in shaping our engineering organization as we scale one of the fastest-growing companies in the world.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

- Own full-cycle recruiting across software, machine learning, research, infrastructure, security, and leadership roles.

- Partner directly with the VP of Engineering, CTO, and Engineering Managers to define headcount plans, role outcomes, success profiles, and the hiring bar. Prioritize reqs against business goals.

- Build top-of-funnel through targeted passive outreach, talent intelligence, referrals, events, and Mercor’s own product (structured screens, automated work samples, and calibrated rubrics).

- Source and close passive, high-bar candidates. Lead with a compelling narrative, handle objections, and drive offer strategy and negotiations aligned to leveling, comp bands, and market data.

- Design assessments that predict on-the-job performance. Define competencies, calibrate rubrics, and keep raising signal quality.

- Coach hiring managers and interviewers on structured interviewing, leveling, and decision hygiene.

- Operationalize hiring systems. Track and optimize pass-through rates, time-in-stage, source yield, and diversity signals, and report weekly and quarterly with clear metrics and narrative.

- Champion speed and quality: drive SLAs for same-day debriefs and fast offers, and maintain a consistently strong candidate experience.

- Maintain a mapped bench of high-potential talent for critical and future roles.

- Build Mercor’s brand with top technical talent through campaigns, content, communities, and events. You’ll be a face of Mercor for the engineers and researchers we want most.

- Partner on dashboards, metrics, and process automation in Ashby and other recruiting systems.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

- 6+ years of full-cycle technical recruiting, ideally in high-growth or deep-tech environments.

- Deep familiarity with technical roles: SWE, MLE, Research, Applied AI, Security, Infrastructure, and TLM.

- A proven track record of sourcing and closing passive candidates for high-bar IC and leadership roles.

- Demonstrated ability to build and scale hiring systems, identify the right metrics, and make data-driven decisions.

- Fluency with structured interviewing, competency rubrics, and recruiting analytics.

- Strong communication skills and the ability to influence senior stakeholders, including the VP of Engineering, the CTO, and cross-functional leaders, at pace.

- Commitment to inclusive hiring and an excellent candidate experience.

- Familiarity with Ashby, or the ability to pick up new tools quickly.

NICE TO HAVES

- Experience as a founding technical recruiter or early-stage builder.

- Experience hiring ML researchers or research engineers at an AI lab.

title: Product Manager - Administration & Governance
description:
About Supabase

Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Product Manager, Administration & Governance to join our Product Team and make Supabase the default starting point for software built inside a company.

Supabase already spreads from the bottom up: someone has an idea, creates a project, and builds something useful. Inside most companies, Supabase starts the same way: someone has an idea, creates a project, and builds something useful. The next step is making that momentum company-wide: one platform where anyone can start building, and where IT can see what’s running, who owns it, and what it costs.

You’ll own how companies run Supabase as their internal development platform: approved by IT and easy for anyone in the company to use. You’ll make it possible for people and the agents they work with to start building without waiting on infrastructure, while giving platform, IT, and security teams the controls they need to say yes. The goal is to make the approved path the easiest path, from an early experiment to a production application, with the controls companies need built in.

WHAT YOU’LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR

- Own the product strategy and roadmap for internal innovation, from a company’s first IT-approved rollout to adoption across teams and business units.

- Make getting started self-service, whether someone creates a project in Supabase, through an internal developer portal, or with an agent. Give builders the access and infrastructure they need without a ticket for every project.

- Steer scattered usage into a manageable company-wide platform. Give companies one view of everything they run on Supabase. Shape how ownership, delegated access, and boundaries work so teams can move independently as usage grows.

- Partner closely with platform, IT, security, and finance teams to understand what it takes to approve Supabase and keep it approved. Translate their needs into practical identity, policy, audit, and spend controls that don’t slow builders down.

- Define the path from experiment to production, including project ownership, access, and the guardrails that change as an application becomes important to the business.

- Work with Engineering, Design, Sales, and Customer Success to turn early customer rollouts into a repeatable experience, rather than a new custom integration for every company.

- Define what success looks like, instrument it end to end, and let the data guide what gets built next-from time to first project and self-service adoption to production usage and expansion across the company.

YOU MIGHT BE A GOOD FIT IF YOU

- Have 7+ years of product management on developer tools, infrastructure, or internal developer platforms.

- Have built self-service products that developers love and platform or IT teams trust. You understand both the person trying to ship an app and the team responsible for how it runs.

- Can reason about identity, permissions, organization boundaries, and usage attribution, and turn those systems into workflows people can actually understand.

- Have a strong point of view on how agents change who can build software inside a company and what an internal development platform needs to make that possible.

- Know your way around controlled experimentation and data analysis, and can connect easier adoption to sustained product use.

- Are biased toward speed and would rather ship, learn, and iterate than perfect a spec.

- Build with what you own and form opinions through first-hand use, from creating a project to configuring the policies around it.

- Use AI tools to compress research, drafting, and feedback synthesis so you can focus on judgment calls.

- Work async by default, making decisions in writing in a fully remote tea
